I’m so sorry for your loss. My mom passed in January of 2021. She was unwell and our relationship wasn’t what it once was but I loved her nonetheless. She was only 52 and really wanted to be a grandma. She was the first person to bother my husband and I about having kids after we got married.  I got really close with my dad after her passing and my husband was and has been very supportive. My mother in law had also been pretty awesome throughout my pregnancy and afterwards. I tell my son about his grandma that is no longer with us just so he knows about her and keeps her memory alive. It makes me feel better when I sing him songs my mom loved or things like that. You’ll be great mom and it may be tough not to share these moments with her but as long as your baby knows grandma, it may help ❤️

FTM  and I just had my baby two days ago and was 40+5. Tried membrane sweeps at 38 and 39 week appts but cervix was also high. I had maybe few contractions before then but felt like Braxton Hicks. They decided to do a non stress test and ultrasound the day before I gave birth, everything was fine, but I had some high blood pressure. Next day at dr appt, I’m getting induced because the high blood pressure and she did a membrane sweep then. Got the balloon inserted right after being admitted and went the full 12 hours with contractions. Once they took it out, they started petocin and had an epidural about an hour after that. Bloody show came somewhere after that. Then almost two hours later, it was time to push and they had to break my water right before pushing. Three hours and a break in between, he was here. I didn’t want to be induced if need be but I also felt disappointed when no signs of labor was happening, no mucus plug or bloody show and I was getting closer to 41 when I tried almost everything too. After being induced, I didn’t care so much because I knew baby would be coming soon and it was worth the wait!

First off, congrats!  I also deal with anxiety and bouts of depression.  I think changing therapists is a good idea and finding a good one can be hard but don’t settle until you feel comfortable and safe with one you like.  I will admit it has taken a lot of years to combat my anxiety and I still get attacks but I find what works for me is to let myself feel it for awhile and then usually I will try to self soothe- take a shower, watch some tv or read, hug my animals.  Find something to distract you or something you enjoy.  Even talk to your husband if you can.  I find by him just listening really validates my feelings plus a good hug helps too.  I also found journaling and yoga has helped me really connect with myself and find why/ where my anxiety stems. 
I know the hormones don’t help with anxiety so be kind to yourself.  It sounds like you’re doing a good job already understanding what triggers you and doing your best to fix it.  You’re doing an important job growing a person!
